issues.title: [Bug]: xml template with interpolation produces a read-only value
issues.output:
true
error: cannot mutate readonly XML element
        at main(i1698.bal:8)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. The BIR is correct: evalTemplate[xml] with escaped insertions, assigned to x of type xml. At run time, execEvalTemplateExpr (runtime/internal/exec/non_terminators.go:319) builds the value with values.ParseAsXMLValue(..., XMLTemplateMode), which returns a read-only element. A clean-context check of the spec agreed it is VALID: only an xml template inside a const-expr is read-only, and elements are selectively immutable. So it is a runtime bug. The fixture corpus/bal/subset10/10-xml-navigation/lang-xml-errors-v.bal relies on the current behaviour and needs updating with the fix. No duplicate found (#1628 is about isolation and is different).

issues.title: [Bug]: value:cloneWithType returns the same xml value instead of a copy
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. lang.value cloneWithType returns the source xml (also when nested in map<xml>) instead of a deep copy. A clean-context check of the spec agreed it is VALID: cloneWithType copies like Clone, and Clone recursively copies mutable sequence values. Lang library behaviour, so langlib. No duplicate (#1471 and #1005 are different).

issues.title: [Bug]: error constructor accepts a non-definite contextually expected type
issues.edge_case_reason: Needs an untyped error constructor whose contextual type is a union of two distinct error types, a rare combination.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. The program compiles with no diagnostic and builds a plain error that is neither DA nor DB. A clean-context check of the spec agreed it is VALID: §6.17 requires the applicable contextually expected type to be definite, and DA|DB is not. The front end is missing a diagnostic, so it is frontend. No duplicate (#1375 is related: distinct (A|B) is rejected for the same definiteness rule).

issues.title: [Bug]: toString/toBalString render cycles as [...]/{...} instead of ...[N]/...
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. A clean-context check of the spec against §5.9.5 (the 'cycle detected' row) agreed it is VALID: toBalString should print ...[N] and toString a bare .... It noted a slight ambiguity about N in the indirect-cycle case, but the target-container reading (N=0) is the natural one. Lang library behaviour (lang.value toString/toBalString), so langlib. The corpus expectations in 10-value/tobalstring-v.bal and 03-list/20-v.bal need updating with the fix. No duplicate (#979 is about objects, #1259 about xml).

issues.title: [Bug]: data.xmldata: a long general-entity chain overflows the stack instead of hitting the depth limit
issues.reproducer: (issue reproducer: needs ballerina/data.xmldata from PR #1415 plus a generated 3,000,000-entity chain.xml; see the issue)
issues.output: Not reproducible on main: ballerina/data.xmldata does not exist on main yet (PR #1415, head dc553a312, is open and unmerged). Read the PR head code instead: (*dtd).resolve in lib/stdlibs/ballerina/data.xmldata/0.0.1/go1.27/native/dtd.go recurses through walkReferences into each nested entity, and checks cost.depth > maxEntityDepth only after the recursion returns. So the Go stack depth grows with the chain length, as the issue says.
issues.reasoning: A review finding on unmerged PR #1415. Main is not affected, but reading the PR head code confirms the bug: the depth limit is checked after recursing, not before. Valid: the library documents a depth limit of 500, and an uncatchable fatal stack overflow is wrong. Standard library, so library + triage-lib. Recommend keeping it open and linking it to #1415, or fixing it in that PR before merge. If the policy is to track only bugs on main, close it as 'not planned' and move it to a review comment on #1415 instead.
